brief: Gold squeezed violently higher after a five-week, $19.5 billion speculative selling washout (final week alone: $8 billion, split $5.2 billion long liquidation and $2.8 billion fresh shorts, driven largely by Other/Non-Reportable traders). Extreme downside-hedging demand (25-delta put-call skew at its 85th percentile) and sizeable CTA shorts preceded the reversal, and short covering is adding fuel. Falling oil, dollar weakness and Chinese demand are additional tailwinds. Goldman's Privorotsky argues gold may be an inverse oil trade: EM central banks, pressured by high energy bills, may have sold or paused gold buying, so falling oil eases that pressure and gold catches a bid, a theory the note calls unproven. Separately, Goldman flags Chinese traders buying gold and selling copper as an AI-investment-cycle hedge, not a broader equity rotation, but warns the trade is increasingly dangerous and vulnerable to reversal. SocGen highlights Tether as a new structural buyer, holding 146.5 tonnes as of June (projected 161 by September), growing 31% annualized versus 13.6% for ETFs and 1.8% for central banks. The open question is whether this is short covering or genuine fresh buying. Gold must reclaim the 50-day MA ($4,205) to confirm a persistent bullish move; the 200-day MA sits near $4,500.
